sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Sammamish, WA?
sections.html:
The three usual routes in Sammamish are a standard listing, a sale by owner and a cash sale as-is. A cash sale is the one built for speed, because the buyer does not wait on a mortgage approval, but the price will reflect the condition of the house and the shortcut.

Sammamish is a high-value market. The Census Bureau's median value of owner-occupied housing for 2020 to 2024 is $1,407,300, and 82.6 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, so most sellers here own a single-family home on a plateau lot rather than a rental. The city's estimated population slipped 2.0 percent between the April 2020 base of 67,457 and 66,110 on July 1, 2025.

  • Hire an agent if the house shows well and you can handle a few weeks on the market.
  • Take a cash offer if you are relocating, settling an estate, or dealing with deferred maintenance.
  • Sell it yourself if you are comfortable preparing the disclosure form and the closing documents.

Whatever you choose, compare offers using the same four terms: price, closing date, closing cost split, and repair credits.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Sammamish?
sections.html:
Sammamish sits on a plateau east of Lake Sammamish about 20 miles east of Seattle, with the Snoqualmie Valley to the east. It covers 24.04 square miles, of which 3.61 are water, and neighbors Issaquah to the south, Redmond to the northwest and Bellevue across the lake. Beaver Lake and Pine Lake are the two largest lakes in the city, and Yellow Lake lies in the Klahanie area.

The plateau stayed mostly rural until suburban homes, shopping centers and schools arrived in the 1970s and 1980s. A 1991 vote to join Issaquah and a 1992 incorporation vote both failed. After frustration with county development rules, voters approved incorporation in 1998 and the city was officially incorporated on August 31, 1999. Sammamish annexed Klahanie on January 1, 2016.

The city approved plans for a denser Town Center in 2008. The first residential buildings were completed over the following decade, and construction on 38 townhomes in a later phase began in 2024, with more townhomes and 600 apartments planned. Sammamish does not have its own post office, the closest being in Redmond. Eastside Fire and Rescue provides fire service, and the city contracts with the King County Sheriff's Office for police.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads do Sammamish buyers ask about?
sections.html:
School district boundaries split the city along Southeast 8th Street. Everything north of it is in the Lake Washington School District, with Eastlake and Tesla STEM high schools and Inglewood and Renaissance middle schools. Everything south is in the Issaquah School District, with Issaquah and Skyline high schools and Beaver Lake, Pacific Cascade and Pine Lake middle schools. A small eastern area belongs to the Snoqualmie Valley School District. Say which district applies when you list the house, since buyers filter by it.

Major roads are East Lake Sammamish Parkway along the lakeshore, 228th Avenue through the business district and Issaquah-Pine Lake Road. State Route 202 leads to Redmond and Interstate 90 runs through Issaquah to the south. King County Metro runs a route linking Sammamish to Redmond, Issaquah and Mercer Island station, and the South Sammamish Park and Ride has 265 stalls. The 11-mile East Lake Sammamish Trail was completed in 2023.

The Census reports a mean travel time to work of 29.3 minutes, so commute questions are common. A buyer who works in Redmond will weigh the drive on SR 202, while one headed to Seattle will think about I-90 and the light rail connection at Mercer Island.

sections.html:

With 90.6 percent of residents in the same home a year earlier, turnover is low, and the buyers who do come are mostly families looking for space and schools. With 28.6 percent of residents under 18, bedroom count, yard size and the school district carry weight in pricing.

sections.h2: How does Sammamish weather and zoning affect a sale?
sections.html:
Winters are cool and wet, with the wettest months being November, December and January, and summers are warm and dry. Snowfall is rare. Recorded extremes run from minus 8 degrees Fahrenheit in February 1950 to 113 degrees in June 2021. Roof, gutters, drainage and crawl spaces get the most attention from inspectors, and the state disclosure form asks about roof leaks in the past five years, standing water and drainage problems.

Zoning details can add value. The city's R-4 zone allows up to 4 dwelling units per acre, a maximum floor area ratio of 50 percent for single-family homes and 40 percent hardscape coverage. A detached accessory dwelling unit in R-4 needs setbacks of 15 feet in front and 5 feet on the sides and rear, with a 24-foot height limit.

Accessory dwelling units are broadly allowed. Sammamish permits up to two on a lot with a detached single-family home, whether attached, detached or converted from an existing structure. A detached unit is capped at 1,000 square feet, and an attached unit can be up to 50 percent of the house or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger. No extra parking is required when the property already has four or more spaces. If you are selling a lot with potential, mention these rules, and tell buyers to confirm current standards with the city.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs, taxes and disclosures in a Sammamish sale?
sections.html:
The state real estate excise tax is paid by the seller in most sales, due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the first $551,000 is taxed at 1.1 percent and the next slice up to $1,551,000 at 1.28 percent. At the Census median value of $1,407,300, that works out to $6,061 on the first bracket and $10,960.64 on the remaining $856,300, a state total of $17,021.64 before the local rate. This is an illustration of the arithmetic, not a quote. Ask your escrow officer or King County for the local rate and for the brackets that apply if you close before January 1.

Property tax bills follow the parcel. Under RCW 84.56.020, tax statements go out by March 15 when the county meets its deadlines, and each statement must describe the senior exemption and deferral programs. Half is due April 30 and half October 31 for bills of $50 or more. Treasurers may offer payment agreements for current or delinquent taxes, so ask King County Treasury about your balance before closing.

For the buyer's side of the file, give the disclosure statement within five business days of contract acceptance. It includes a notice that restrictive covenants based on race or other protected classes are void and unenforceable under RCW 49.60.224, and asks about homeowners' association dues, special assessments, shared common areas and recorded covenants. If your home is in an HOA, get the documents ready early.

A short checklist before you sign a contract:

  • The deed and loan payoff statement.
  • HOA bylaws, dues and any pending special assessments.
  • Permit and final inspection records for additions or any accessory unit.
  • The most recent King County property tax statement.

faqs.q: How quickly can I sell a house in Sammamish, WA?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close as soon as title work is finished, and many sellers choose the date. A listing normally takes longer because of showings, inspections and buyer financing. Get the closing date in writing from any buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Sammamish house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell without making repairs, but you still need to complete the state disclosure form unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies. A buyer who purchases as-is will account for the condition in the price.

faqs.q: Does the school district matter when I sell in Sammamish?
faqs.a: It matters to buyers. Addresses north of Southeast 8th Street are in the Lake Washington School District and those south are in the Issaquah School District, with a small eastern area in the Snoqualmie Valley district. Confirm the district for your address.

faqs.q: Can a buyer add an accessory dwelling unit to a Sammamish lot?
faqs.a: Often yes. The city allows up to two ADUs on a lot with a detached single-family home, with a 1,000 square foot maximum for a detached unit. Setbacks and height limits depend on the zone, so a buyer should confirm the standards with the city.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Sammamish home?
faqs.a: Half is due April 30 and the remainder October 31, as RCW 84.56.020 provides for bills of $50 or more. King County Treasury collects the tax, and the closing agent usually prorates it between buyer and seller.
